newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian train station masters call off strike.
newsitem.headline: Italian train station masters call off strike.

text.p: Italian railway station masters have called off a strike that was due to begin at 2000 GMT on Tuesday, their union said.

The UCS trades union said the strike, which would have lasted until 0500 GMT on Wednesday, was called off after the government said it would include the union in talks with other trades unions on reforming the railway system.

The government said on Tuesday it would meet railway unions on February 19 to discuss a reform of the state-run Ferrovie dello Stato railway and try to avoid more strikes threatened by the unions later this month.
Railway travel was paralysed at the weekend when all train workers staged a 24-hour strike to protest at a plan by Prime Minister Romano Prodi to reorganise the railway system.
The plan would split the railway company in two by the end of 1997 -- one managing the rail lines and infrastructure and the second the train and rolling stock.
Unions are unhappy with the bulk of the plan and a move to abolish free rail tickets for staff and their families.
